newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Women paid less than men in EU.
newsitem.headline: Women paid less than men in EU.

text.p: Women in the European Union earn on average a fifth less than male counterparts, the European Commission said on Thursday.

In a report outlining progress on equal opportunities to mark International Women's Day on Saturday, the Commission said between 20 and 40 percent of full-time women workers are recorded as low paid in the different EU countries.
The report, unveiled by the EU's Social Policy Commissioner Padraig Flynn at a news conference, said over 70 percent of womens' jobs are in the services sector, where they occupy the lowest grades.
Women make up 83 percent of low-security and low-prospect part-time workers.
Fewer than 30 percent of small and medium-sized companies in Europe are run by women, who are responsible for only one third of business start-ups, it said.
According to an opinion poll released in parallel, the fact that women are trailing behind in the job market does not mean they are less interested in work than men.
The poll also showed that most people gave family life priority over other aspects of their lives.
According to the poll, which is a study of 21,300 people throughout Europe, in two thirds of European couples the woman does most of the household chores.
"This is more pronounced the older the couple concerned, where the women doesn't work and in cases of lower education levels," the Commission said in a statement.

The EU executive concludes from the data that despite a relatively complete legal framework on equal pay and equal treatment for women and men, EU law is not always properly applied and EU citizens need greater help to know their rights and seek redress.
